Tue Nov 10diplomacy

Russia and Ukraine hold first US-brokered talks since February as Russian strikes hit Ukraine's power grid

Russian, Ukrainian and US negotiators began two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, their first three-way meeting since February, hours after Russian air attacks struck 10 Ukrainian regions and killed two people, Reuters and the Associated Press reported.

Tue Nov 10diplomacy

Rubio presses G7 partners in Paris to help protect Strait of Hormuz shipping

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged other nations on Tuesday to "step up" and help protect shipping from Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, but said he made no headway with his Group of Seven counterparts at talks in Paris, the Associated Press reported.

Tue Nov 10elections

Israel's new Knesset is sworn in as Eisenkot tries to form a government

All 120 members of Israel's 26th Knesset were sworn in on Tuesday in Jerusalem, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot works to build a coalition to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the BBC and The Times of Israel reported.

Tue Nov 10global-institutions

UN rights council postpones US review to January after Washington skips it again

The United States did not take part on Tuesday in its scheduled Universal Periodic Review before the UN Human Rights Council, and the council rescheduled the review for January 18-29, 2027, Anadolu Agency and the Washington Examiner reported.

Tue Nov 10conflict

Clashes in Bangladesh as supporters of ousted leader Sheikh Hasina demand her return

Police in Bangladesh fired tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse supporters of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday, as the banned student wing of her Awami League held nationwide protests demanding her return from exile in India, the BBC reported.

Mon Nov 9conflict

Trump says US land blockade of Iran is in effect as Iran reports tankers hit mines near Hormuz

President Donald Trump said on Sunday that Task Force Iron Gate, a US effort to stop Iran moving weapons and sanctioned goods over its land borders and the Caspian Sea, was "in full force and effect," while Iran said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters and Al Jazeera.

Mon Nov 9diplomacy

EU and E3 to join US-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi despite Kremlin objections

The European Commission and European Council will send a joint team of senior officials to the US-hosted Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, alongside France, Germany and the UK, according to Euronews and NPR.

Mon Nov 9global-institutions

UN COP31 climate summit opens in Turkey as Guterres warns of a 'new age of climate extremes'

The UN's annual climate conference, COP31, opened on Monday in Antalya, Turkey, and runs until November 20, as UN Secretary-General António Guterres said, "We have entered a new age of climate extremes," according to the UNFCCC, AFP and the Guardian.

Mon Nov 9elections

South Africa's ANC stays largest party with 30.76% in final local election results

South Africa's Electoral Commission declared the November 4 municipal elections free and fair on Sunday, with the ANC winning 30.76% of the vote, down from 45.59% in 2021, and the Democratic Alliance 24.64%, according to the government news agency SAnews and Reuters.

Mon Nov 9conflict

Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses and regains outside power in 27th such outage, IAEA says

The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine lost its last external power line on Sunday and ran on backup diesel generators for reactor cooling until power was restored hours later, the International Atomic Energy Agency said, according to Reuters and Interfax-Ukraine.

Sun Nov 8public-safety

Poland mourns six killed in Krakow square shooting; prosecutors treat it as terrorism

Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday after a 24-year-old gunman killed six people and wounded 15 in Krakow's Main Square on Saturday, AP and the BBC reported.

Sun Nov 8conflict

Aramco building in Riyadh damaged by debris after Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles

Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said falling debris damaged an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh on Sunday, with no injuries or deaths reported, Reuters and Al Jazeera reported.

Sun Nov 8rail

Two trains collide south of Cairo, killing 7 and injuring more than 100

A train bound for Fayoum crashed into the rear of a stationary Cairo-to-Aswan train in Giza's al-Ayyat district on Sunday, killing at least seven people, Egyptian authorities said, according to AP and the BBC.

Sun Nov 8diplomacy

Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina and meets President Milei

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires on Sunday for the second leg of his South American tour and was greeted by President Javier Milei, Vatican News and AFP reported.

Sat Nov 7elections

Israel's president tasks Eisenkot with forming a government, sidelining Netanyahu

Israeli President Isaac Herzog said Saturday he was giving opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a governing coalition after the Oct. 27 election.

Sat Nov 7conflict

US forces disable cargo ship in Gulf of Oman after blockade breach attempt

U.S. Central Command said Saturday that U.S. forces disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored warnings and tried to violate the naval blockade against Iran.

Sat Nov 7conflict

Iran's Revolutionary Guard says self-imposed missile range limit has been lifted

An IRGC spokesman said Saturday that Iran's long-standing self-imposed limit of about 2,000 kilometers on ballistic missile range has been lifted, without confirming that longer-range missiles are already deployed.

Sat Nov 7conflict

Russian strikes wound civilians in Ukraine ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks

Drone and missile attacks struck across Ukraine on Saturday, wounding people in multiple regions as Kyiv and Moscow prepared for U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

Sat Nov 7elections

Paraguay swears in Alliana after Peña impeachment over bank collapse

Pedro Alliana was sworn in as Paraguay's president on Friday after the Senate impeached Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, and prosecutors placed Peña under house arrest.

Fri Nov 6politics

Paraguay's Congress presses impeachment of President Peña after he offers to resign over a bank collapse

Paraguayan President Santiago Peña offered to resign on Thursday over the collapse of Ueno Bank, but Congress declined to accept it, and the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, according to Al Jazeera and AP.

Fri Nov 6elections

Israel's president to name a candidate to form a government on Sunday after 67 lawmakers back Eisenkot

Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday he will task a lawmaker with forming the next government on Sunday, after factions totaling 67 lawmakers recommended Gadi Eisenkot and 46 recommended Benjamin Netanyahu, according to Al Jazeera and The Times of Israel.

Fri Nov 6elections

South Africa's ANC on course for sharp drop in municipal election vote share as counting continues

With 71% of votes counted, South Africa's African National Congress was on 32% of the municipal election vote against 25% for the Democratic Alliance, according to Reuters; the ANC would be down about 14 percentage points from 2021 if the figures hold.

Fri Nov 6diplomacy

Pope Leo begins 12-day Latin America tour three weeks after lung cancer surgery

Pope Leo left Rome on Friday for a trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru running from November 6 to 17, about three weeks after lung cancer surgery, according to Vatican News and AP.

Thu Nov 5elections

Israel's president accepts election results and opens talks on who will form the next government

Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday accepted the certified results of the October 27 parliamentary election as legally binding and began consultations with parties on who should be asked to form a government, according to AP and Al Jazeera.

Thu Nov 5aviation

Bomb threats force diversions and emergency landings across Europe for the second time this week

Airlines across Europe received a new series of bomb threats on Thursday, leading to diversions, escorted flights and emergency landings, though inspections had found no explosives, according to Reuters, AP and the BBC.

Thu Nov 5conflict

Tanker hit by two projectiles off Qatar, UK maritime agency says, as Iran reports ship fires in Hormuz

A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, late on November 4, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said, adding that the status of the crew and the damage were unconfirmed.

Thu Nov 5diplomacy

Ukraine and Western partners meet in Brussels on reconstruction and security guarantees as airstrikes continue

Ukrainian officials met representatives of the United States, the European Commission, Britain, France, Germany, NATO and the World Bank in Brussels this week on Ukraine's postwar recovery and security guarantees, while Russia and Ukraine traded overnight airstrikes, according to AP and Ukrinform.

Mon Nov 2global-institutions

UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years as Security Council deadlocks

The UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) stopped operating on Sunday after its mandate expired at midnight Saturday, when the Security Council failed to agree on renewing it, according to the UN, AP and NPR.

Mon Nov 2security

Ukraine and Russia say hackers hijacked their emergency alert apps to send fake nuclear warnings

Ukraine's Air Alert app sent false warnings of radiation, chemical attacks and street fighting late Sunday, and hours later Russia's emergencies ministry said its own warnings app had suffered a "massive cyberattack", according to the BBC, AP and AFP.

Mon Nov 2conflict

Israeli forces pull out of Hebron after operation launched over the killing of two soldiers

Israel's military said its soldiers withdrew on Monday from the area of its operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron, and Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said Palestinian security forces had taken full control and displaced families could return, according to AFP, Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency.
